2608.18758.title: Epistemic Subordination: Generative AI and the Infrastructure of Knowledge
2608.18758.paper_summary: Generative AI does not merely produce biased outputs. It encodes the majority's way of knowing as the default infrastructure of knowledge itself. We call this epistemic subordination. The training process compresses the full breadth of human expression into a single probabilistic model whose statistical baseline reflects the languages, assumptions, and cultural frameworks of the dominant culture. Minority epistemologies are not excluded but absorbed: present in the training data, yet structurally subordinated in the output. The result is not a collection of discrete biases that can be audited and corrected. It is an epistemic condition embedded in the architecture from which all outputs emerge. This unified harm cuts across three legal domains -- anti-discrimination law, cultural and linguistic rights, and democratic viewpoint pluralism -- and each fails to address it for the same structural reason: existing law regulates downstream, at the level of decisions and applications. The remedy must match the site of harm. If epistemic subordination is produced at the level of model training, then law must learn to govern at that level.
2608.18758.paper_summary_zh: 生成式人工智慧不僅僅產生偏見的輸出。它將大多數人的認知方式編碼為知識本身的默認基礎設施。我們稱之為認識上的從屬。訓練過程將人類表達的全部範疇壓縮成一個單一的概率模型，其統計基線反映了主導文化的語言、假設和文化框架。少數群體的認識論並不是被排除，而是被吸收：它們存在於訓練數據中，但在輸出中結構性地處於從屬地位。結果並不是一組可以審核和修正的離散偏見。這是一種嵌入所有輸出產生架構中的認識狀態。這種統一的傷害橫跨三個法律領域——反歧視法、文化和語言權利，以及民主觀點多元主義——而每一個領域都因為相同的結構性原因未能解決這個問題：現有法律在決策和應用層面進行調節。補救措施必須與傷害的發生地點相匹配。如果認識上的從屬是在模型訓練層面產生的，那麼法律必須學會在該層面進行治理。
2608.18758.author: Gilad Abiri et.al.
